subject: mathematics
question_text: Write the definitions of singular and non-singular matrices, and give an example of each.

recall_prompt: Give both definitions in terms of the determinant, and one example of each.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Define singular and non-singular
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both definitions are about the determinant and nothing else. Say square once, because only a square matrix has a determinant.
lines: Let A be a square matrix.
A is called singular if det A = 0.
A is called non-singular if det A ≠ 0.
Only a non-singular matrix has an inverse.

recall.must_convey: That a square matrix is singular when its determinant is 0 and non-singular when its determinant is not 0.
accept: singular means the determinant is zero
non singular means the determinant is not zero
a square matrix with determinant zero is singular
determinant zero aithe singular, zero kaakapothe non singular
only the non singular one has an inverse

steps.why: The determinant is the single test, so the two words simply name the two cases det A = 0 and det A ≠ 0. The link to the inverse follows at once, because det A sits in the denominator of A⁻¹ = (Adj A)/(det A).
common_mistakes: Swapping the two, so det A = 0 is called non-singular.
Saying singular means the matrix has no rows or columns repeated.
Using the definition on a matrix that is not square.
steps.memory_tip: Singular is the odd case, det A = 0; every other square matrix is non-singular.

steps.label: Give an example of each
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write the determinant out for each example. An example with no determinant shown proves nothing.
lines: det A = 0, so A is singular.
det B = −2 ≠ 0, so B is non-singular.

lines.text: ∴ A is singular, B is non-singular

recall.must_convey: That one example has determinant 0 and is singular, and the other has a non-zero determinant and is non-singular.
accept: one two two four has determinant zero so it is singular
one two three four has determinant minus two so it is non singular
work out both determinants and name each matrix
modati determinant zero, rendo determinant minus two
the first is singular and the second is non singular

steps.why: The two examples differ in one entry, so they show that being singular is a property of the numbers and not of the shape. Writing each determinant out is what turns an example into evidence.
common_mistakes: Giving two examples but working out neither determinant.
Thinking the zero matrix is the only singular matrix.
Labelling the examples the wrong way round.
steps.memory_tip: A quick singular example: make one row a multiple of the other, and the determinant is 0.
